title: How does one surgeon do 2,000 operations?
principle: One standard way of working cuts cost and mistakes.

screens.text: Let me tell you about an eye hospital in Madurai. Aravind Eye Hospital does cataract operations, which help people see clearly again. An Aravind surgeon does about 2,000 a year; India's average is 250. And its patients have half as many problems after surgery as patients in Britain. Guess how.

screens.prompt: How do Aravind's surgeons do so many operations while keeping patients safe?

options.label: Its doctors work many more hours
Everyone follows the same steps each time
It uses costly machines from abroad

screens.why: Everyone follows the same steps each time. While a surgeon operates on one patient, helpers prepare the next. The surgeon does the most important steps, and trained helpers do the rest in the same order. When everyone knows the order, a missed step is easier to see.

screens.title: Standard work
screens.text: This is called standard work: you write down the best way to do a job, so everyone follows it. Toyota made it famous in its factories. It doesn't mean working harder. When everyone follows the same steps, you find mistakes faster and fix them for everyone. Let's try it here.

screens.title: Now look at your bakery
screens.text: It's August, your home bakery's fifth year. Your sister and cousin now bake with you: about 30 cakes a week at ₹850 each, costing ₹400 each. But your chocolate cakes taste different, and about 3 a week come out wrong, because each of you bakes differently.

screens.prompt: You bake 30 cakes a week. 3 go wrong, and baking each again costs ₹400. How much do these mistakes cost in 4 weeks?
screens.why: Exactly. 3 cakes × ₹400 = ₹1,200 a week, so in 4 weeks that's ₹4,800. You earn ₹450 on each ₹850 cake, so you've lost more than ten cakes' worth of profit, all because there are three different ways to bake.

wrong.a: That's the cost for one week: 3 × ₹400 = ₹1,200. In 4 weeks, the mistakes cost ₹4,800.
wrong.c: You worked out 3 × ₹850 × 4. But ₹850 is the selling price. Your loss here is the cost of baking again: 3 × ₹400 × 4 weeks = ₹4,800.

screens.prompt: Let's write your chocolate cake on one card. I'll show you six notes. For each one, tell me: should it go on the card?

items.text: Weigh 60 grams of cocoa on a scale
Add sugar until you like the taste
Bake it just like Mummy used to
Ready when a knife in the middle comes out clean
Beat the mixture until it looks good

screens.why: Exactly. A standard card gives steps anyone can follow and check: weights, temperatures, times and tests. "Until you like the taste", "like Mummy used to" and "until it looks good" mean different things to different people. Write "beat for 4 minutes" instead.

screens.prompt: Here are five steps to get everyone working the same way. They're mixed up. Put them in the right order.
steps: Bake your best cake and weigh every ingredient
Write down the weights, times and checks on a card
Teach your helpers and watch each person bake once
Check a few cakes from each person using the card
When someone finds a better way, test it and change the card
screens.why: Exactly. First, find your best way and measure everything. Then write it down, teach everyone and check their cakes. The last step matters most, because the card can change: when someone finds a better way and it works, everyone follows the new card.

screens.prompt: Your cousin didn't follow the card. She guessed how much sugar to add, and her cake came out perfect. Was her method good?

options.label: Yes, because this cake came out well
Yes, because the customer liked the cake
No, because she might guess wrong next time

screens.why: Right. Remember Unit 1: judge the thinking, not the luck. A cake can come out well even when someone guesses, but that doesn't make guessing a good method. A clear card helps all three of you bake cakes that taste alike.

wrong.a: Her cake came out well this time. But remember Unit 1: judge the thinking, not the luck. One good result doesn't prove that guessing works. Next time she may guess wrong, and nobody will know why.
wrong.c: The customer liked one cake, but one good result does not prove the method works. Judge the thinking, not the luck. Guessing the sugar may fail next time, and nobody will know why.

screens.prompt: Your sister tried beating the mixture 5 minutes longer on one cake, and it came out lighter. She tells you. What should you do?

options.label: Test it on a few cakes before deciding
Ask her to keep following the old card
Let her use it only for her cakes

screens.why: Exactly. Standard work can improve. Your sister tried a new way once and told you, which is a good start, but one cake is not enough. Test it on a few cakes, and if it keeps working, change the card so everyone follows the better method.

wrong.b: The card is the best way so far, not forever. Try her idea on a few cakes. If it really works, put it on the card, so every cake gets lighter.
wrong.c: Then her cakes and yours taste different again. Test her idea, and if it works, change the card for everyone.

screens.setup: It's late August. A café wants 10 chocolate cakes every Friday, all tasting and looking the same. Because it buys many, it pays ₹700 per cake. Each costs ₹400 to make, so you would earn ₹3,000 a week. Your sister and cousin will bake most of them.
screens.question: How do you get ready for the café?

options.label: Bake all 10 cakes yourself each week
options.outcome: All the café's cakes come out the same, and you earn ₹3,000 a week. But you bake late every Thursday, and after two weeks your home orders start getting late.
options.why: You made the cakes right, but only you know how. If every cake depends on you, your business cannot grow beyond what you can bake yourself.
options.better: Write a card, bake the first batch with your helpers, and check it.

options.label: Bake the first batch together using a card
options.outcome: You write the card and bake the first batch together. One cake fails your check, so you earn ₹2,600 that week, and you fix that step on the card. After that, all 10 cakes turn out alike every week. You earn ₹3,000 a week, and your Thursday nights are free.
options.why: Exactly. The card let three people bake one cake. Checking the first batch found the weak step early, and the fix reached everyone at once.

options.label: Give them the card and check the cakes they make
options.outcome: The card helps, but you never watched them bake. Your cousin uses a heaped spoon of cocoa instead of weighing 60 g. Every Friday one cake tastes wrong, so you bake it again and earn ₹2,600 a week. The café is happy, but you spend Friday mornings fixing cakes.
options.why: Writing the card was a good start. But you didn't bake together, so each person could understand it differently. Show them every step, and watch them do it once.
options.better: Write the card, bake the first batch together, and check it.

screens.text: Same idea, different shop: three tailors cut shirts in different ways, so the sleeves never ___. One written ___ way could fix this.
screens.why: Exactly. Same job, three ways, three results. Write the one best way down, teach it, and the shirts match, just like your cakes.

summary: Standard work: one written best way for each job, which everyone follows.
Write things anyone can check: grams, temperatures, times and tests.
When someone finds a better way, test it and change the card for everyone.

cards.front: Three helpers bake the same cake three ways, and some cakes fail. What fixes it?
options: Taste every cake at the end
cards.back: Standard work: one written best way that everyone follows.

cards.front: Which line belongs on a standard recipe card?
cards.back: Write things anyone can check: grams, temperatures, times.

cards.front: A helper finds a better way to do one step. What now?
options: Test it, then change the card for all
Tell her to follow the card
cards.back: A standard is the best way so far. Improve it for everyone.
